title: The AASM Manual for the Scoring of Sleep and Associated Events, Version 3
sourceRole: current scoring, staging, respiratory, cardiac, movement, and technical terminology
authority: controlling scoring terminology for this study system
apaReference: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
copyrightBoundary: Glossary term names are inventoried. Learner definitions and memory clues are original Sleep Pathways Guild summaries rather than reproduced AASM glossary prose.

items.definition: The beginning of the first epoch scored as sleep rather than wake.
items.memoryClue: Sleep onset starts with the first scored sleep epoch.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A combined signal produced by electrically summing the thoracic and abdominal PVDF respiratory-belt signals.
items.memoryClue: PVDFsum combines thorax + abdomen.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A distinct 11-16 Hz burst lasting at least about half a second, usually strongest over central EEG derivations.
items.memoryClue: Spindles are a core N2 marker.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Conjugate, irregular, sharply peaked eye movements with a rapid initial deflection, characteristic of REM sleep but also possible during wake.
items.memoryClue: REMs are fast, conjugate EOG deflections.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Repetitive jaw-muscle activity during sleep involving tooth grinding or clenching and associated clinical consequences.
items.memoryClue: Bruxism is sleep-related jaw activity.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Repeated conjugate eye movements with alternating slow and fast phases produced while reading or visually scanning.
items.memoryClue: Reading movements are a wake EOG clue.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A disorder in which REM sleep without normal muscle atonia is associated with dream-enactment behavior.
items.memoryClue: RBD links REM-without-atonia with dream enactment.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Smooth, rolling eye movements usually seen during drowsiness and the transition from wake to N1 sleep.
items.memoryClue: Slow rolling eyes suggest drowsiness/N1.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A sequence of breaths with increasing respiratory effort or inspiratory flattening that ends in an arousal but does not meet apnea or hypopnea criteria.
items.memoryClue: RERA = flow limitation/effort ending in arousal.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: EEG slow activity in the frequency and amplitude range used by the AASM to identify N3 sleep.
items.memoryClue: Slow-wave activity drives N3 scoring.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.term: Sustained muscle activity (tonic activity) in REM
items.definition: Persistently elevated chin EMG during REM sleep compared with the expected low REM atonia baseline.
items.memoryClue: Tonic REM activity means sustained loss of normal atonia.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The number of scored respiratory events per hour of monitoring time in a home sleep apnea test.
items.memoryClue: REI uses monitoring time, unlike AHI which uses sleep time.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A sinus rhythm that exceeds the AASM sleep tachycardia rate threshold for the patient’s age group.
items.memoryClue: Use the sleep-specific rate threshold.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A belt-based method that detects changes in thoracic and abdominal circumference to estimate respiratory effort.
items.memoryClue: RIP belts track chest and abdominal effort.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An airflow sensor that detects temperature differences between inspired and expired air.
items.memoryClue: Thermal sensors are strong apnea detectors.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: EEG activity in the theta frequency range.
items.memoryClue: Theta is slower than alpha and faster than delta.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An airflow-estimate signal derived from calibrated respiratory inductance plethysmography.
items.memoryClue: RIPflow estimates airflow from belt signals.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The electrical sum of thoracic and abdominal respiratory inductance plethysmography signals.
items.memoryClue: RIPsum combines thorax + abdomen.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An infant EEG pattern with alternating bursts of higher-voltage slow activity and lower-amplitude mixed activity during quiet sleep.
items.memoryClue: Trace alternant alternates high-voltage bursts and quieter intervals.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Brief sharply contoured EEG waves maximal over central regions, commonly appearing during the transition into N1 sleep.
items.memoryClue: Vertex waves are central sharp transients of light sleep.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Short irregular bursts of EMG superimposed on low muscle tone, commonly seen in REM-related muscle recordings.
items.memoryClue: Transient = short EMG bursts.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A run of at least three rapid consecutive beats with QRS complexes wide enough to meet the AASM wide-complex criterion.
items.memoryClue: Fast rhythm + wide QRS.
references: Troester, M. M., Quan, S. F., Berry, R. B., et al. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events: Rules, terminology and technical specifications (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
